We explain why Syria and Israel really aren’t getting along; why Israel continues to occupy parts of southern Syria; and why the odds of an outright conflict only seem to be rising with time.

Our mission is to explain news and politics in an impartial, efficient, and accessible way, balancing import and interest while fostering independent thought.

TLDR is a completely independent & privately owned media company that's not afraid to tackle the issues we think are most important. The channel is run by a small group of young people, with us hoping to pass on our enthusiasm for politics to other young people. We are primarily fan sourced with most of our funding coming from donations and ad revenue. No shady corporations, no one telling us what to say. We can't wait to grow further and help more people get informed. Help support us by subscribing, engaging and sharing. Thanks!

snippet.description:
Economy Foundation Module – Lecture 2 | NCERT Economics | Types of Economy, Demand & Supply, Elasticity and Equilibrium

Welcome to Lecture 2 of the Economy Foundation Module. In this class, we cover important basic concepts of Economics using an NCERT-oriented approach to help students build a strong foundation for competitive examinations.
Understanding the fundamentals of Economics is essential for UPSC CSE, State PCS, RAS, BPSC, MPPSC, SSC and other government examinations. This lecture focuses on economic systems, demand and supply, elasticity, and market equilibrium.


✅ Types of Economy
- Traditional Economy
- Command Economy
- Market Economy
- Mixed Economy
- Basic differences between economic systems

✅ Demand and Supply
- Meaning and basic concepts of Demand
- Meaning and basic concepts of Supply
- Demand Curve and Supply Curve
- Factors affecting Demand and Supply
- Basic understanding of changes in market demand and supply

✅ Elasticity of Demand
- Meaning of Elasticity
- Price Elasticity of Demand
- Elastic and Inelastic Demand
- Factors affecting elasticity
- Basic applications of elasticity in Economics

✅ Market Equilibrium
- Meaning of Equilibrium
- Equilibrium Price and Equilibrium Quantity
- Interaction between Demand and Supply
- Basic understanding of changes in market equilibrium

Who Should Watch This Class?
This Economy Foundation Lecture is useful for:
- UPSC CSE Prelims and Mains aspirants
- State PCS examinations such as RAS, BPSC and MPPSC
- Students beginning their Indian Economy preparation
- Competitive exam aspirants who want to strengthen their Economics basics

How to Prepare Economics Effectively
Start with basic concepts, understand diagrams and economic relationships, make short notes, and practise topic-wise MCQs after completing the lecture. Revising definitions and graphical concepts regularly will help improve conceptual clarity.

NCERT-oriented Economics Foundation Module.
Watch the complete lecture, revise the concepts and practise questions to strengthen your Economics foundation.
